D1 — Sampling, DT Signals and System Properties (L02–L03)

Why this matters in the exam: Sample Test 1 puts this material in Q1 (sampling and stem plot, 5 marks), Q2 (sequence operations and energy, 4 marks) and Q3 (system properties, 4 marks). That is 13 of its 20 marks. These are quick marks if your method is clean, and that is the point of this refresh. Your Test 1 Reference already holds the full theory, so this pack is about doing it fast and correctly under time pressure.

1. The core ideas

4. Traps that cost marks

  • Reading as 480 Hz. Divide by to get 240 Hz.
  • Reconstructing before reducing into . You just get back and lose the aliasing marks.
  • Dropping the sign when a term aliases to a negative frequency (T1 Q2: ).
  • Evaluating numerically with rounding error instead of noting that it is exactly 1 (Sample Test Q1(a)).
  • Using instead of , or rounding down (636 levels needs 10 bits, not 9).
  • Missing the arrow. Every sequence answer must mark or list the indices. Applying in the wrong order: scaling first, then shifting by instead of .
  • Calling time-varying. It is a constant gain. Only would vary with time.
  • Calling linear because it “looks like a straight line”. It fails the test.

7. Add to your open-book reference sheet

SAMPLING  f0=F0/Fs, w0=2*pi*F0/Fs. Reduce w0 into (-pi,pi]. Nyquist RATE = 2Fmax.
  Alias: Fa = F0 - k*Fs in (-Fs/2, Fs/2].  sin(-a) = -sin a (sign flips), cos(-a) = cos a.
  Ideal DAC: substitute n = Fs*t AFTER reducing.  cos(2*pi*k*n) = 1 for integer k.
PERIODIC (DT)  f0 = k/N in lowest terms -> N.  Leftover pi -> aperiodic.  Sums: N = LCM(Ni).
ADC  D = (xmax-xmin)/(L-1);  b = ceil(log2 L);  bit rate = b*Fs;  |eq| <= D/2;  Fmax = Fs/2.
ENERGY/POWER  E = sum|x|^2 (finite -> energy, P=0).  P = lim 1/(2N+1) sum_{-N}^{N}|x|^2.  u(n): P=1/2.
SEQUENCES  u(n+a)-u(n-b) = 1 on [-a, b-1].  x(n-d): shift right.  x(Mn): keep multiples of M.
  x(n/L): zeros between samples.  x(an+b): substitute each n directly.  ALWAYS mark n=0.
PROPERTIES  Static: only x(n).  Linear: x=0 -> y=0, no x^2/|x|/cos x/offset.
  TI: [input delayed, explicit n untouched] vs [every n -> n-d].  Explicit n coefficient -> TV.
  Causal: no x(n+k), check n<0 too.  Stable: bound |y| by Mx, or u(n) -> infinity disproves.
  One concrete counterexample disproves a property.
CORRELATION  rxy(l) = sum x(n)y(n-l) (no flip).  rxy(l) = ryx(-l).  rxx even, rxx(0) = Ex.
  Radar: d_hat = argmax |ryx(l)|;  d = round(2*Fs*r/c).
